subject: FintechCo multi-region performance & competitive follow-up
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechco.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: FintechCo multi-region performance & competitive follow-up

Hi Alex,

Great to speak today — thanks for walking us through FintechCo's latency and residency requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:  

Summary from today's discovery
- Primary goal: Serve latency-sensitive customer-facing scoring (p50 < 120ms across US/EU) and guarantee data residency for EU workloads.
- Traffic split: ~65% US, 30% EU, 5% APAC (growth to APAC in Q4).
- Current concerns: hyperscaler vendor lock, unpredictable tail latency, and unit cost at peak.

Proposed tests (attached in redwood-test-plan.xlsx):
1) Multi-region perf run: Redwood hosted endpoints in us-west, eu-west, ap-northeast for the same workload and request mix you shared. We'll run 100k requests/day over 48 hours to capture steady-state and tail metrics.
2) Competitive baseline: run the same workload against Bedrock (us/eu) and Vertex AI endpoints to compare p50/p95/p99, cold-start behavior, and unit cost per 1M tokens.
3) Data residency verification: confirm EU-only processing path (no US egress) for the EU subset and provide audit logs/snapshots.
4) Failure/fallback scenarios: simulated region outage to validate automatic routing to dedicated fallback and measurable impact on latency.

Next actions and owners
- Redwood (Camila/Jordan): schedule the runs, provision temporary test keys for Bedrock/Vertex and collect metrics. Deliverables: perf report + redwood_vs_hyperscalers-summary.pdf. (ETA Aug 14)
- FintechCo (Alex/Sarah): provide final list of representative prompts, a 48-hour traffic window, and confirmation of IP ranges for in-region traffic.

I've attached the test plan and a short matrix that maps our tests to your success metrics. If this looks right, we'll schedule the runs early next week and loop in Eng for any network whitelisting.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0193

Thanks Camila — good recap. Two quick notes from our competitive test perspective:  

1) For Bedrock/Vertex parity, we should lock model variants (e.g., 8-bit quantized where applicable) so we're comparing apples-to-apples on compute. I'll spin up the baseline variants and capture the exact model ids used so the comparison is reproducible.
2) Let's include a tokenized cost model: measure cost per 1k tokens + effective tokens/second at target p50 for each region. FintechCo cares about unit economics as much as latency.

I'll take point on running the Bedrock/Vertex comparisons and will post a short runbook in the shared Drive folder before we kick off.

-Jordan

Camila, Jordan — thanks for the clear plan. A few clarifications from our side:  

- Prompts: we'll send the representative prompt set (10 example prompts + distribution file) by EOD Aug 12.
- Data residency: for EU traffic we need to be able to show an auditable log that data was processed in-region and not routed to the US for any stage of inference. Is Redwood able to provide signed audit logs for the test runs?
- Hyperscaler keys: we can provision test accounts but need a short runbook for how Redwood will use those credentials and whether they will be stored beyond the test window.

Also, curious about your fallbacks — would Redwood's fallback to a different region incur request replays (double-processing) or is it a queued failover? We need to ensure idempotency constraints won't be violated in our scoring pipeline.

If you can address the above, we'll confirm the test window and IP whitelists.

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Head of Platform Engineering | FintechCo
alex.chen@fintechco.com

Hi Alex — short answers and next steps:  

- Signed audit logs: yes — for the test runs we can provide per-request signed audit records that indicate processing region, timestamps, and the serving node id. We'll include a sample audit export in the perf report.
- Hyperscaler credentials: we will only use provided test keys for the explicit comparison runs and will delete/stage-limit keys immediately after tests. I'll include a short credential handling addendum in the Drive runbook.
- Fallback behavior: traffic routing uses an atomic redirect — requests that fail in-region are retried to the fallback endpoint with a configurable retry policy. We do not replay successful requests. For your scoring pipeline, we recommend idempotency tokens for critical endpoints; we'll support the header and show how retries surface in the audit logs.

Next steps:
- FintechCo: send prompts + IP ranges by EOD Aug 14.
- Redwood: we'll start provisioning test endpoints and publish the runbook + schedule (targeting Aug 17 kick-off).

I'll follow up with the perf report and the summary PDF after the runs (ETA Aug 21).

Appreciate the partnership — will circle back once runs complete.

Best,
Camila
